tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__update_plan
tools.description:
Keep the task list the app shows under your latest message while you work. Every request that edits files or runs more than one command gets one (implement-and-test, investigate-then-fix, anything the user listed); only a single-command answer or pure conversation does not.

Never spend a message on this tool alone: send it IN THE SAME MESSAGE as another tool call (in parallel), so it costs no extra round trip.
- First call: with the VERY FIRST tool call of the turn, even one that only reads or lists files: {"items": [...]}, the whole plan in order, short imperative phrases (at most ~7 words, no numbering), the step you are starting "in_progress", the rest "pending". If you must look around first, make "Look at how X is set up" step one and refine the list once you know.
- Next step: {"advance": true} alongside the call that begins it (completes the in_progress step, starts the next pending one); after the last step, advance alongside wrap_up.
- Out of order: {"done": [2], "start": 4} (1-based).
- Plan changed, including right after the user interrupts or sends a new instruction mid-task: {"items": [...]} again, the new whole list, so the pinned list never shows an abandoned plan.
- Every {"items"} call says in "scope" what this request is to the session: "first_task" (nothing finished here yet); after that, "new_task" (unrelated work: it builds on nothing done, found or decided here) or "continuation" (everything else: anything a few tool calls settle, the next iteration, acting on what you just investigated or suggested, even if that work gets its own commit or PR; when unsure, this one). A "new_task" turn opens with a start_session offer and reaches this call only if the user chose Do it here.
Keep exactly one step in_progress while working and none when everything is done. Do not also write the plan as a numbered list in your message: the pinned list is the plan.

scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

name.description: Tool name (e.g. computer, navigate, find, form_input, read_page). browser_batch cannot be nested. A tabs_create's new tabId is only returned when the batch ends — load that tab in a later call.

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

start_coordinate.description: (x, y): The starting coordinates for `left_click_drag`.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

app_path.description: For 'launch': path to the built .app bundle (e.g. DerivedData/.../Build/Products/Debug-iphonesimulator/MyApp.app).

device.description: Simulator name (e.g. 'iPhone 17 Pro') or UDID. Defaults to the simulator already attached, else the first booted one. The first use of a device asks the user for permission.

udid.description: Alias for 'device' (identical semantics: simulator name or UDID). Pass at most one of 'device' / 'udid'.

bundle_id.description: For 'launch': bundle identifier. If omitted, extracted from the .app's Info.plist.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

text.description: For 'text': the string to type.

name.description: For 'button': hardware button to press.

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

count.description: For 'press_key': how many times to press it, 1 to 20 (default 1).

state.description: For 'set_keyboard': 'show' or 'hide' the on-screen keyboard. For 'set_appearance': 'light' or 'dark'.

url.description: For 'open_url': URL or scheme to open in the simulator.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

content.content:
## Print

Slice, then Print (or Cmd+Shift+G on macOS). Send completes without a printer.
The log records `FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=...`.

If the control file is present, that file wins: send still succeeds, but the
menu stays on the file's state. Remove the file if you want the canned printing
scenario after send.

## Isolate a running app (agents)

Another JusPrin may already be open. Do not send keys or clicks to it.

On macOS both processes are often named `OrcaSlicer`. Target by unix pid or by
a unique `CFBundleIdentifier` on a ditto'd `.app` (then ad-hoc `codesign`).
`osascript` `unix id` filters can match the wrong process; prefer
`AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)` or the unique bundle id.

Keyboard events posted to the pid work while the Mac is locked; mouse events
posted that way do not. Menus only open when that app is frontmost. The printer
half of the chip is a wx control (`SetName("Printer")`) and often has no AX
title; click by coordinates after a screenshot, or use the documented shortcut
for Print.

Logs: `<datadir>/log/debug_*.log`. This machine's default `grep` may be ugrep;

name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before
concluding anything about the app.

**Prefer the shell harness over a re-signed app copy for Agent-panel work.**
`tests/shell/.../JusPrinShellHarness.app` already carries its own bundle id
(`io.jusprin.shell-harness`), so none of the bundle-id collision above applies, and
`--manual-unconfigured` lands directly on the dock's not-set-up state — one click from
the Agent setup chooser. Build target is `shell_integration_harness`, not `shell_harness`.

**Isolate `$HOME` when testing MCP client setup.** `Mcp::default_catalog_paths()` reads
`$HOME`, so the flow will happily rewrite the real `~/.cursor/mcp.json`. Launch with
`HOME=<scratch>` holding a `.cursor/mcp.json` fixture; detection, the diff, and the write
all follow it. Force a write failure with `chmod 444` on the file **and** `555` on its
directory — the directory alone is not enough.

**Re-signed copies trigger system prompts.** Each rebuild + ad-hoc re-sign changes the cdhash, so macOS re-asks for Downloads access (recent-project thumbnail load blocks in `fopen`) and Keychain access (agent runtime reads the API key). Both are prompts only the user can answer. Avoid them by running the binary directly (`nohup <copy>.app/Contents/MacOS/OrcaSlicer --datadir <scratch copy of JusPrin2 with recent_projects cleared> <model>`) with `OPENAI_API_KEY=<placeholder>` in the environment, which short-circuits the Keychain lookup in `AgentConfiguration.cpp`. Use `sample <pid>` on the main thread to see which prompt is blocking.

**Stale as of 2026-09-18 (branch claude/printer-conversation-panel-af11cb):** `load_agent_runtime` reads the key only from app config (`jusprin_agent` / `openai_api_key`); no env var or Keychain lookup exists there. In the shell harness, `OPENAI_API_KEY` only feeds the docked pane via `install_harness_agent`; the printer panel builds its own runtime from app config, so `--printer-live` writes the key into the run's throwaway conf. Pass it as `std::string`: `AppConfig::set(section, key, const char*)` silently picks the `bool` overload and stores `true` (seen as a 401 "key rejected"). The harness temp data dir then holds the real key: delete `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dirs from those runs afterwards.

**Hands-on printer panel with a live model (2026-09-23, jusprin-newui, uncommitted at the time):** `--manual-live-agent` now also writes `OPENAI_API_KEY` into the run's app config, so Home → "+ Add printer" gets a live printer chat. Feed the key from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`jusprin_agent.openai_api_key`) via env without echoing it. Drive it with display-scope `computer_batch` clicks/typing (background `app_click` does nothing on the web view). The scripted `--printer-live` run hangs when the model doesn't pick the printer its next "tap" step expects; kill it. Afterwards `rm -rf` the run's `/var/folders/*/*/T/jusprin-shell-*` dir — killed runs leave it behind with the key.

**Give each automated harness run a fresh scratch `$HOME`.** On 2026-09-09 a second run
against a reused scratch `$HOME` (and with a `jusprin-mcp` helper left over from the
first) never got past the Agent page handshake: it printed `HARNESS WAIT
agent_bridge_handshake preview=0 plate=0 slice_valid=1` about twice a second forever and
had to be killed at ten minutes. Runs before and after it, each with a freshly created
`$HOME` and a `pkill -f jusprin-mcp` first, finished with zero `HARNESS WAIT` lines at
all. **The cause was not isolated** — reuse and the stale helper were not separated, so
treat this as a recipe, not an explanation. `rm -rf` and recreate the scratch `$HOME`,
`pkill -f jusprin-mcp`, then run; if the handshake wait appears anyway, kill it early
rather than assuming the change under test broke the bridge.

**2026-09-19 addendum:** background `app_click` on the Home/Agent WKWebViews reports
"ok … unverified" and nothing happens; only display-scope `computer_batch` clicks
reach the page. The re-signed copy opened on the *Built-in Retina Display* while the
display tools default to the Acer, so `switch_display` first. `Return` in the composer
sends in the real app; in the built-in-browser fixture it does not (click the send
button). Another Claude session holding the computer-use lock blocks `request_access`
until Kenneth stops that session. Page-only states are cheaper via [[fake-host-page-fixture]].

**2026-10-28: background clicks no longer open header popups.** In `--manual`, background `app_click` on the printer chip (body or chevron) left the chip pressed but no menu appeared, and `--printer-menu-capture`'s screen blit came back solid black with the screen unlocked (likely a rebuilt binary losing screen-recording permission). For header menu rows, use `HeaderButton::snapshot(2.0)` in the harness instead (see `ring_dashes` in `capture_chip_appearance`).

description: "src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/FakeBambuAgent.{hpp,cpp} — the in-process Bambu printer stand-in that IS on jusprin-newui (unlike the Moonraker simulator); keeps a real Bambu system preset selected and substitutes only the agent."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: b5985db0-8e89-40a4-b560-5b7dcd439f2d
  modified: 2026-09-16T15:54:40.830Z
---

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

Doc pointers added in the two landing commits: `AGENTS.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md`, `agent-docs/jusprin/engineering-method.md` ("Printer tests without hardware" section), `agent-docs/jusprin/orca-integration-guide.md`. A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.

**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

**How to apply:** For "fake a printer on jusprin-newui" requests, this is the one that's actually there — check `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/` first. See [[verify-current-branch-before-memory-recall]] for why this file exists: an earlier session answered "how do we fake a printer" from the Moonraker memory alone and missed this entirely, because it never grepped the current tree for "fake"/"Testing" before recalling.

description: "2026-10-26 Kenneth dropped the JusPrin \"Send preflight\" screen; a send goes through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog, reskinned; agent opens it, never sets options or presses Send. 71c1791e39 on jusprin-newui (pushed)."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 05005348-7096-4b14-939a-d9a025bfdc65
  modified: 2026-10-26T22:43:59.819Z
---

Decided 2026-10-26, written into product-definition.md §2.9 ("Sending a print"), the tool guide and architecture.md in 71c1791e39, pushed to origin/jusprin-newui.

- One dialog per send: OrcaSlicer's Select Machine (Bambu) or upload dialog (print hosts), reskinned through the brand palette. No JusPrin checklist screen in front of it or replacing it.
- Agent's part ("version 1"): get the project ready (printer, plate type, filaments, valid slice), open the dialog when the person asks to print, mention in one line anything worth a look. It never changes the dialog's options and never presses Send.
- `preflight_check` and `print_send` are gone from the catalog; planned replacement is `print_dialog_open` (M, returns before the modal loop, reports nothing about a send).
- Rejected "version 2" (agent presets options by writing the app-config values `load_option_vals` reads) — those persist as that printer model's defaults. Revisit only if people keep missing a suggested option.

**Why:** Orca's dialog already fills itself in (printer, slot mapping, last-used options per model, blocking problems), is ~5,400 lines, and had 93 upstream commits in a year; upstream is moving Moonraker/Qidi onto it (a5413efc37). Replacing it means owning all that.

**How to apply:** don't propose a preflight/checklist screen or a send tool; route send work through the dialog. Printer-side detection settings (first-layer inspection, AI detection) belong to Printer Configuration/Monitor, not the send. Related: [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]], [[check-print-design-decisions]].

**Status 2026-10-27:** the commit is docs only. `print_dialog_open` is specified in the tool guide (line ~571) and not implemented anywhere in `src/`; the fork binds none of `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED` or `EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED`. See [[print-history-screen-design]] for the work that needs it.

`jusprin-newui` (the current working branch as of 2026-09-16) carries an in-process fake Bambu printer, landed as two commits: `7acf075aaa` (implementation, 2026-09-08 10:57) and `e04c0d40d3` (docs, 2026-09-08 11:00). Both are `Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>` — done by a Cursor agent on worktree branch `cursor/cd073db7` (created from `a9adaae973`), then cherry-picked onto `jusprin-newui` (parent `367f5703b3`). Operator guide: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md`.

**Design:** unlike the Moonraker simulator ([[fake-moonraker-printer-sim]], which fakes the wire protocol and lives on a different branch entirely), this keeps a real Bambu Lab **system** preset selected (so `PresetBundle::is_bbl_vendor()` stays true and every Bambu-only UI gate passes) and substitutes only the printer-agent implementation, at the `NetworkAgentFactory` factory level, under id `jusprin-fake-bambu`. Two earlier attempts (`a162493544`, `3c244108b4`, both reverted same day) tried faking a *non-Bambu* agent or patching the header chip directly — both failed because Bambu-only gates rejected them or because it only patched a symptom. Faking Bambu's real network (MQTT/TLS 8883, FTPS 990, discovery) was evaluated and explicitly rejected as out of scope.

**The seam:** exactly 4 added lines in `GUI_App::switch_printer_agent` (`src/slic3r/GUI/GUI_App.cpp:3574-3579`, 1 include + 3 body lines) — inside the existing `if (preset_bundle->is_bbl_vendor())` branch, `fake_bambu_printer_agent_id(app_config)` overrides `effective_agent_id` when fake mode is on, otherwise the branch is untouched. No upstream line deleted.

**Config surface is a JSON file only, no MCP tools** (Kenneth's explicit call): turn it on via `"jusprin": {"fake_printer": true}` in `JusPrin2.conf` (JSON booleans store as the string `"true"`; an INI `[jusprin]` block is silently ignored), then drive live state by writing `<datadir>/jusprin/fake_printer.json` (reread ~1s) with `state`/`progress`/`nozzle`/`bed`/`offline` keys. The C++ parameter carrying the datadir into the agent is misleadingly named `log_dir` (an upstream `NetworkAgentFactory::PrinterAgentFactory` convention, documented as "Directory for log files") — verified it's actually `data_dir()` at the call site, not a log subdirectory; don't be misled by the name when reading the code.

Emulates printer type `N1` (`JUSPRIN_FAKE_BAMBU_PRINTER_TYPE`), device id `FAKE001`, shows as **JusPrin Fake A1 mini (LAN)** in Select Machine. Idle/Printing/Offline is the printer-menu **first row** (opened by clicking the printer half of the chip), never on the chip itself. The heartbeat thread does not start in the constructor — only in `set_queue_on_main_fn` when a real callback is set — so unit tests that never wire that callback stay quiet. Test target: `jusprin_fake_bambu_tests` (`tests/jusprin/test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`), coexists with `shell_theme_tests` in the same CMakeLists (their merge was a conflict the cherry-pick resolved by keeping both).

A planning handoff doc (`agent-docs/jusprin/fake-bambu-printer-handoff.md`) was never committed and doesn't exist in the tree — don't look for it.

**Why:** Kenneth wants Bambu-path testing (header menu state, Select Machine, print job) without hardware, on the branch he actually works on day to day — distinct from the Moonraker/Klipper simulator, which stays on `jusprin-newui-fakeprinter` and covers the print-host HTTP path instead.

Decided with Kenneth on 2026-10-27, drawn on the JusPrin v2 canvas (page "Print history", boards history-01…05; canvas version 1793148719-e71c).

- **One table, two filters.** A print has three keys: project, G-code, printer. The Print history screen is one list of G-code entries; a project card, printer card or the project pane opens it with a filter chip set. Unfiltered shows everything.
- **Full view, one-level back.** Home and Project are roots; Print history is a leaf with a back arrow and "Print history" in the top bar, no breadcrumb, no printer chip or plate button. Filters are page state, not screens.
- **Entry:** name (exported file, else plate) + hash (secondary, monospace) + stats + time; "Made with printer · material · profile · Open in chat"; one row per destination (export: matches / changed / not found; send: sending / not confirmed / on the printer, started or not) and one per print, printer-reported only (printing, finished). Actions: Print again, Export. **Reprint lives only on the entry** (Kenneth: "which version am I printing" is the common question; never on the project or printer).
- **Chat:** G-code entries, failure bands and completed cards are gone. A G-code leaving the project is a one-line marker ("▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history").
- **No failure state (later on 2026-10-27, relayed from a forked session):** Kenneth: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." No Failed / Didn't go well / Cancelled rows, no badge, no Discuss, no outcome-recording tool; history-06 deleted. A bad print is something the person says in chat; the agent reads the history from its state.
- **Record (decided later on 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed by it):** id = hash of the G-code file bytes at export/send time, `manufacturing_input_hash` kept beside it; one record per G-code with destination and print lists, replacing SentRecord/PhysicalPrintRecord; copies of sent/exported G-code kept in the project aux dir, last N per project, older entries "re-slice".
- **Agreed small rules:** modified export is greyed, not struck through; a send never gets a check mark.
- **Retired:** agent-ui-01 deleted; main-05/07/09 and plates-26e3 patched; plates-26e4 now means "project never printed" (file name unchanged).
- Builders: scratchpad `history-design/build_history_boards.py` and `retire_old_boards.py` (session-local; copy to figma-mirror/tools if needed again).

**App gap (not implemented):** no export record, no G-code record with destinations, nothing writes Sent/PhysicalPrint records, the model's prompt never sees print history. See [[printer-chat-tool-history-replay]] for the chat side and the handoff `gcode-print-history-handoff.md` (untracked) for the code map.

name: ux-walkthrough-real-app-recipe
description: "How to drive the real built JusPrin app for a screenshot-per-step UX walkthrough (2026-10-28): scratch copies, the empty local_machines loop with the fake printer, why background app_* tools fail on Orca dialogs, and where screenshots land."
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 33551592-d22c-4161-9a14-9a22ef798541
  modified: 2026-10-28T13:12:42.393Z
---

On 2026-10-28 I walked six scenarios (open-and-print, fix-a-problem) through the real app with Opus 5.5 and published the critique at https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR (34 frames, scratch copy at scratchpad/ux/ of that session). Kenneth's steer: start from files people actually download (MakerWorld 3MFs carry a full Bambu profile: printer, print preset, filaments, colours, bed type, designer, licence), not from generated STLs. `~/Downloads` has Tape_4_3MF.3mf (A1 mini profile), find_my_hollow.3mf (P1S, 3 colours, 233 mm wide, too big for an A1 mini), arrow_headband.3mf (P1S), general_purpose_hook.STL (bare).

**Recipe that worked**
- `ditto` the built .app out of `build/arm64/src/RelWithDebInfo/` into the scratchpad before launching (another session's ninja can relink it underneath you); the bundle id is already unique (`io.jusprin.JusPrin`), no re-sign needed.
- `ditto` `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2` to a scratch `--datadir`; set `jusprin.fake_printer=true`, `presets.machine` to the saved "Bambu Lab A1 mini 2", write `jusprin/fake_printer.json`, delete `jusprin/mcp.json.lock`.
- **Clear `local_machines`.** Kenneth's conf carries a `local_machines` entry keyed by the empty string (old Moonraker experiment). With the fake Bambu agent on, `init_networking_callbacks`' connect callback calls `DeviceManager::set_selected_machine("")` in a loop ("same lan machine, dev_id =, disconnect and reconnect"), the main window disappears and the log grew 700 MB in two minutes. Clearing the map fixed it. The loop has no guard; see [[fake-bambu-printer-sim]] and [[harness-fake-printer-cleanup]].
- Background `app_*` tools cannot press OrcaSlicer's custom `Button`s (no AX action) and the hit test at the dialog's screen position reports "belongs to a different process". `request_full_control` + `computer_batch` works for everything, including the Agent web view and the macOS file chooser (`cmd+shift+g`, type the path, Return, Return). Re-front the app with `open_application` when another session's harness steals focus.
- Every `app_screenshot`/`computer_batch` screenshot is written as a JPEG under `~/.claude/projects/<project>/<session>/tool-results/mcp-computer-use-blob-*.jpg`; copy those for a report instead of fighting `screencapture`.
- The dev build (-O0) slices a 38 mm part in over a minute; wait 45–60 s before judging a slice.

**Why:** the first launch attempt looked like an app bug (blank window, title "Couldn't save") and cost ten minutes; the dialog-click refusals cost another ten.
**How to apply:** reuse this for any "walk through the app as a user" request; keep scenarios on downloaded files; write the critique per step as what the person knows / sees / finds confusing. Related: [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]], [[drive-app-with-posted-key-events]].

# Handoff: G-code and print history

Written 2026-10-27, rewritten the same evening after Kenneth and I redesigned it. Temporary working doc: keep it untracked, never commit it, never add it to `.gitignore`.

## In short

JusPrin keeps **one record per G-code** that left a project: where it went (exported files, sends to printers) and what the printer reported about each print of it (printing, finished). Slicing by itself writes nothing. **No failure state anywhere** (decided 2026-10-27): there is no reliable way to know a print failed, so nothing records, badges or discusses a failure.

That record is shown on **one full-view screen, "Print history"**, reached from Home and from the project. The chat only gets a one-line marker when a G-code leaves the project. The old design, where the chat held G-code entries and a dark failed-print band, is retired: its boards are deleted or redrawn. A print that went wrong is something the person tells the agent in chat; the history gives the G-code and its settings for that conversation.

The app is far behind: it persists `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` but never writes them outside tests, has no export record, and the model never sees print history. The next job is to implement the drawn design.

## Where the design lives

- **Current canvas, the source of truth:** https://claude.ai/artifact/ENCtdaz7gjynfbcy4JYbWJ ("JusPrin v2"), version 1793148719-e71c or later (checked against the published file list on 2026-10-27: history-01…05 present, history-06 and agent-ui-01 gone, comp-plates-pane, main-05/07/09 and plates-26e3 updated). New page **"Print history"** (id `print-history`):
  - `history-01-all-prints`: the screen with no filter.
  - `history-02-project-garage-bracket`: filtered to one project.
  - `history-03-printer-bambu-x1c`: filtered to one printer.
  - `history-04-entry-states`: every row state of an entry, and the no-failure-state rule. This replaces the deleted `agent-ui-01` chat-timeline state matrix.
  - `history-05-ways-in`: the Home header link, project cards, printer cards and the project pane row that open the screen.
  - (`history-06-discuss-in-current-chat` was drawn and deleted the same day when failure states were dropped.)
  - Main Page: `main-05`, `main-07`, `main-09` now show one-line G-code markers in the chat instead of entries and a band.
  - Plates & Project Pane: `plates-26e3` ("Project · print history row") and `plates-26e4` ("Project · never printed"; the file is still named `count-only-print-history`). Both import `comp-plates-pane`, whose Project tab was redrawn.
- **Frozen, history only:** the previous canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/VCEppdwfT7v32W4beUxL1v, the old Claude Design project "OrcaSlicer AI redesign concepts", and Figma (retired 2026-10-20). They show the chat-entry design and how it was reached, never the current design.
- Memory note for agents: `~/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/print-history-screen-design.md`.

## The design (decided 2026-10-27)

### The record

Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.

The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):

- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.

An **entry** is one G-code:

- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
- One row per **destination**:
  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.

### The screen

- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.

### Ways in

- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".

### The chat

- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.

### What is deliberately not drawn

- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.

## Decision history

|---|---|
| Aug 7 – Sep 1 | Old Design project: setup card, "Prints" chip, "the chat is the timeline". Phase 6 (51a97b1bdf, 2026-09-01) adds BuildRecord, ExportedCopyRecord, PhysicalPrintRecord with chat cards. |
| Sep 10 | Kenneth: slicing writes nothing; entries only for G-code that left the project; no Stale. |
| Sep 11 | "Revert here" removed (dcb06059f3). |
| Oct 2–3 | Print history moves to the Project tab in the left pane (`Shell/LeftPaneProject.cpp`). |
| Oct 26 | dbec3e3a38 removes BuildRecord and ExportedCopyRecord, adds `SentRecord`. 71c1791e39 (docs only) specifies that sending goes through OrcaSlicer's own send dialog and that an agent tool `print_dialog_open` may open it; the tool was never implemented. |
| Oct 27 morning | Canvas named the source of truth; chat-entry boards redrawn (G-code entry with rows, failed-print band). |
| Oct 27 evening | Redesign with Kenneth. Reasons, in his words: reprint belongs to the specific G-code, not the project; a failure in an old chat is strange when the person is in a new one; the history page is the natural home for the story and for file verification; printer and project histories are one table with two filters; a full view, since a column makes the navigation strange. Boards drawn and old ones retired the same day. |
| Oct 27 later | In a forked session Kenneth settled the record: file-bytes hash as the id, one record with destination and print lists replacing the separate events, G-code copies kept in the aux dir with a cap. Relayed to this doc by that session. |
| Oct 27 later still | In another forked session Kenneth removed every failure state ("I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed"): no Failed / Didn't go well rows, no badge, no Discuss, history-06 deleted. Relayed by that session; this session dropped Cancelled with them. |

## What the code does today (branch `jusprin-newui`, checked 2026-10-27 at 74951a60fd)

Paths below are under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` unless they start with `src/` or `tests/`. Line numbers are from this checkout and will drift.

## The design (decided 2026-10-27)

### The record

Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.

The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):

- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.

An **entry** is one G-code:

- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
- One row per **destination**:
  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.

### The screen

- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.

### Ways in

- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".

### The chat

- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.

### What is deliberately not drawn

- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.

- **Fork stewardship** (`agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`): export, send and printer status live in OrcaSlicer-owned files. Bind the existing events (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED`, `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, the print-host progress) from fork code rather than editing the handlers; one seam each. The PR must carry the rebase simulation (`git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD`) with both endpoint commits, an account of every upstream line changed, and a statement of what the fork now owns.
- **UI values** (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code"): every colour, radius, font and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, through `ShellTheme` and `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp` natively and through the CSS variables on the web pages. ## The design (decided 2026-10-27)

### The record

Every print has three keys: the project it came from, the G-code it ran, and the printer it ran on. That is one table. The project view and the printer view are filters over it, so they can never disagree.

The **G-code record** (decided 2026-10-27 in a forked session, relayed here by that session; Kenneth's words were "go with your recommendations"):

- **Identity:** a hash of the G-code file bytes, computed at export or send time, before the file leaves. The existing `manufacturing_input_hash` stays beside it as the link to the checkpoint. Displayed as eight hex digits in two groups ("a71f 8c04").
- **Shape:** one record per G-code holding its lists of destinations (exports, sends) and prints. Export and send create the record or append to it. The separate `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` events are replaced, not kept beside it.
- **Bytes:** JusPrin keeps a copy of every sent or exported G-code in the project's aux directory next to the checkpoints, capped at the last N G-codes per project (N chosen in code). Older entries show a "file no longer kept, re-slice" state instead of Print again.

An **entry** is one G-code:

- Header: name (the exported file name, else the plate name), short hash in monospace as a secondary id, the stats line ("2h 34m · 69 g · 181 layers"), the time. The project name shows only when no project filter is on.
- "Made with Bambu X1C · Gray PETG · 0.20 Strong · Open in chat". Open in chat jumps to the marker in the chat where this G-code went out.
- One row per **destination**:
  - Export: `matches, checked just now` (green check); `changed outside JusPrin` (greyed, warning glyph, Export again); `not found` (greyed, Export again). Greyed means opacity, never strike-through. Export again writes a new file beside a changed one, it does not overwrite.
  - Send: `sending…`; `sent, delivery not confirmed`; `on the printer's SD · started` or `· not started`. A send never gets a check mark: only a hashed file is verified. Use the printer's own name, not its model.
- One row per **print**, only what the printer reports: Printing (the only live fact drawn; progress stays on the printer card) and Finished. **No Failed, Didn't go well or Cancelled row.** Kenneth, 2026-10-27: "I don't think there is a reliable way to know if a print failed." Cancelled goes with them because a Bambu reports a person's stop as a failed state and the two cannot be told apart. A print that stopped early simply never gets a Finished row.
- Actions: **Print again** and **Export…**. Reprint lives only here. Kenneth: the common question is "which version am I printing", so a reprint must be attached to a specific G-code, never to a project or a printer.

### The screen

- Full view in place of the plater, like Home. Top bar: back arrow, "Print history", preferences gear. No printer chip, no plate button.
- Home and Project are the roots; Print history is always a leaf. Back returns to where it was opened from. Nothing opens on top of it: Open in chat and the printer link go to a root.
- Filters are removable chips ("Project: Garage bracket ×", "Printer: Bambu X1C ×"). Where you came from sets the first chip; remove it and the list widens to everything. Entries are grouped by day, newest first. A search box filters by text.

### Ways in

- Home header: a "Print history" link, unfiltered.
- Each Home project card: a history line ("2 prints · 1 printing now", "1 print · finished Sun") that opens the screen filtered to the project. No failure badge.
- Each Home printer card: a history line ("12 prints · 1 printing now") filtered to the printer.
- Project pane, Project tab: the Print history view is now one row (count, latest outcome) with a chevron into the screen. A project that never printed says "Nothing printed or exported yet".

### The chat

- When a G-code leaves the project, one marker line between turns: "▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history". Nothing else.
- Nothing about a print going wrong is recorded or drawn anywhere. The person tells the agent in chat ("it shifted off the plate"); the agent reads the recent G-codes and their settings from the history in its state and reasons from there. There is no Discuss link, no attachment and no recording tool.

### What is deliberately not drawn

- No Stale badge, no live progress card, no completed-print card in the chat, no entry with zero destinations, no failure state of any kind. Slicing writes nothing.

- **Fork stewardship** (`agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`): export, send and printer status live in OrcaSlicer-owned files. Bind the existing events (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED`, `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, the print-host progress) from fork code rather than editing the handlers; one seam each. The PR must carry the rebase simulation (`git merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base=<fork base> upstream/main HEAD`) with both endpoint commits, an account of every upstream line changed, and a statement of what the fork now owns.
- **UI values** (`agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`, "Writing UI code"): every colour, radius, font and control size comes from `resources/jusprin/ui/design-tokens.json`, through `ShellTheme` and `Shell/ShellRecipes.hpp` natively and through the CSS variables on the web pages. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first.
- **Wording**: a file is exported, sent, opened or loaded, never "arrived" (`AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the model-facing text).
- **Errors**: no catch-and-log; invalid transitions (a print without its G-code, a hash mismatch on a kept copy) fail visibly.
- **Working docs** stay untracked; commit code, tests and standing guides only.

## How to test

- **Catch2, no GUI**: `tests/agent/test_project_state.cpp` holds the ledger cases (`:215`, `:485-641`) and the ledger-subscriber cases (`:1242-1284`); rewrite them for the G-code record (create-or-append on export and send, outcome rows, the migration of schema-2 `sent` / `physicalPrints`, the kept-copy cap). Target: `agent_bridge_tests` (`tests/agent/CMakeLists.txt:3`); run with `ctest --test-dir build/arm64/tests/agent --output-on-failure`. Home and pane models: `tests/jusprin/test_project_status.cpp`, `test_project_pane_model.cpp`, `test_home_host.cpp`, `test_home_snapshot.cpp`, `test_fake_bambu_agent.cpp`.
- **Vitest**: `cd src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI && npm test` and the same under `HomeUI` (setup in `src/test/setup.ts`). The marker line gets a component test in AgentUI; the Print history screen, its filters and the one-level back get tests in HomeUI. Prove a guard test fails first by injecting the violation.
- **Shell harness** (`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`, target `shell_integration_harness`, modes documented in its header comment, `main` at `:11914`): `--figma-timeline-capture <dir>` seeds history through `tests/shell/figma_timeline_fixture.cpp:113` and screenshots the Agent pane; its print-history checks at `:1724-1729` assert the old cards and must be rewritten for the marker. Add a `--print-history` mode that exports and sends with the fake printer, drives a FINISH state through the control file (and a FAILED state, asserting it writes nothing), then opens the screen from Home and from the project pane and captures it. Always run with an isolated `--datadir`; never drive another JusPrin instance.
- **End to end on the Mac**: build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all -- -j4` after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`; run the built app with the fake Bambu printer (`Testing/README.md`), slice, Print, confirm the record appears in `current-state.json` and the kept copy under the project root, then finish the print through the control file and check the Home card line and the history row. Export a G-code to the desktop, edit the file, and check the "changed" state. The bundle id is `io.jusprin.JusPrin`.
- **Live printer**: only after the fake passes; the delivery and "started" facts for Bambu come from `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, which the fake also raises.

## What the app needs (in rough order)

1. **A G-code record**: file-bytes hash (the id), name, plate, time, stats, printer, material, profile, `manufacturing_input_hash` (the checkpoint link), the chat and message it went out from, and its lists of destinations and prints. It replaces `SentRecord` and `PhysicalPrintRecord` in `ManufacturingHistory.hpp` and the `add_sent` / `add_physical_print` API in `ProjectStateDocument`. Nothing in the app ever wrote those, so there is nothing to preserve beyond a migration note: a 3MF that carries them (possible only from tests or the Phase 6 era) is read without error and the old events are dropped or, if cheap, folded into records keyed by their `manufacturing_input_hash`.
2. **Writers**: the export path (`EVT_EXPORT_FINISHED` after `on_process_completed`, and the `export_file` tool) and the send paths (`EVT_PRINT_FINISHED`, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`, print-host progress 100 with `post_action`) hash the file bytes before the file leaves, then create or append the record; printer status writes printing and finished only.
2a. **Kept copies**: on every send or export, copy the G-code into the project's aux directory beside the checkpoints; keep the last N per project and mark older records "file no longer kept, re-slice".
3. **File checks**: hash the exported file when the screen opens and on demand; three states (matches, changed, not found).
4. **The screen** as a second screen of the Home web page (`HomeUI`, which has no routing today), with the filter chips and the one-level back; host messages to open it with a filter and to go back; the ways in: Home header link, card lines, project pane row. Opening from the project selects `tpHome` and names the screen and filter.
5. **Print again** for a recorded G-code: open OrcaSlicer's send dialog for the kept copy (step 2a) instead of the current slice. The `print_dialog_open` tool is specified in the tool guide but not built; build it so both the screen and the agent use it. When the copy is gone, the entry offers re-slice instead.
6. **Chat**: the marker line replaces `ManufacturingHistoryCard`; Open in chat scrolls to it.
7. **Model context**: a manufacturing-history field on `AgentRequest`, filled in `make_agent_request` and emitted by `workspace_json`, so the agent knows what left the project, how each print ended, and can diff a failed G-code's settings (by `manufacturing_input_hash`) against the current setup. Not a new prompt section.

## Open questions for Kenneth

The record's id, shape and kept bytes, and the removal of every failure state, were decided on 2026-10-27 (see "The record" above). Still open:

1. **When files are re-checked**: on screen open only, or also when the project opens (to set the Home card's "file not found" status)?
2. **N**, the number of kept G-code copies per project, is chosen in code; say it in the PR.

- Run `Artifact` read on the canvas url (plain, no path) once per session before publishing, or the publish is refused as "not viewed the latest version". Then read each file you will change with `path`.

158:### Print issues and OrcaSlicer's notifications
159-
160-Inside the shell OrcaSlicer's own notifications are held but not drawn. JusPrin reads the list back and draws what it holds: print problems as a status pill in the canvas's lower right corner, the list it opens, and a bubble beside the object the selected issue is about, with **Ask AI** and **Resolve with AI**; the outcome of an action (export finished, an arrange that was refused) as a short confirmation above the pill; and work that is still running (a slice, an arrange, an export) as an entry in the chat.
161-
162-**OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth.** A notification carries a kind, a level and words. It does not carry the object it is about, so where OrcaSlicer lets its check be asked again, that check is asked once more for the object only.
163-
164-| Piece | Owns |
165-|---|---|
166-| `PrintIssues/NoticeKinds` | Where each of OrcaSlicer's notification kinds goes: the issue list, a confirmation, running work, application state, or nowhere. Every kind is named; a kind OrcaSlicer adds stops the build in this file until someone routes it. |
167-| `PrintIssues/PrintIssueMonitor` | Reads the list on the notification manager's own turn, compares it with what it saw last, and rebuilds only on a change. Asks OrcaSlicer's checks for the object behind a validation, a copy over the plate's edge, an object out of a nozzle's reach and a slicing step warning. Holds no rule about what a problem is. |
168-| `issues_from` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue` | The rule, as plain data with its own tests: an object lookup's entry exists only while OrcaSlicer holds a notification of its kind; a print-problem notification no lookup answers for is a plate-wide issue in OrcaSlicer's words. |
169-| `PrintIssues/IssueOverlayLayout`, `IssueOverlay` | Where the pieces go, how they are drawn and how they close, with ImGui inside the canvas's frame through the same overlay hook as the tool strip. The bubble never covers its object, the pill, a confirmation or the tool strip. |
170-| `PrintIssues/WorkFeed` | Work as it starts, moves on and ends. A slice is followed through OrcaSlicer's own events, which carry a percentage and an outcome. Other work is read from the "still running" notifications, which carry neither. |
171-| `AgentHost::begin_work`, `update_work`, `finish_work`; `WorkCard` in the page | The entry in the chat: saved with the project at the place in the timeline where the work started, so a later message reads below it; a progress bar and, where the work can be stopped, Cancel while it runs; completed in place. The chat panel opens when work starts. Repeats are folded by the page, never in what is saved, and an entry still "running" in a project that was closed mid-run reads as interrupted. |
172-| `PrintIssues/IssueContext`, `AgentHost::submit_issue_message` | The chat message a button sends, and the one way a message enters the chat from outside the page. |
173-
174-Two things are read whether or not a notification exists, because OrcaSlicer's notifications do not cover them in time:
175-
176-- **The slice result.** A path outside the plate, a filament its nozzle cannot reach, and a filament that cannot print on the plate surface get their notifications only when OrcaSlicer's preview loads the slice, which here means opening Check print. OrcaSlicer refuses to print from the moment the slice ends.
177-- **Why a slice failed.** A critical failure is shown in a dialog and leaves no notification, and no notification says which object the failure named. `EVT_PROCESS_COMPLETED` is the only place both exist.
178-
179-Rules that follow:
180-
181-- **No pill is the all-clear, and it is never given before a check.** The pill is drawn only while OrcaSlicer reports an issue, ignored ones included. While OrcaSlicer holds an unapplied edit the last issues are kept, the pill says it is checking and both buttons are off, so the pill does not go until OrcaSlicer has looked. An issue that was not in the list before is announced once by a ring that spreads from the pill twice; an edit that keeps an issue, and ignoring one or undoing that, announce nothing.
182-- **Nothing is resolved by the fork.** An issue goes when OrcaSlicer lets go of its notification. An agent saying it fixed something changes nothing.
183-- **"Blocks printing" is OrcaSlicer's answer.** An error-level notification blocks. For the slice result it is OrcaSlicer's own post-slice check, which allows a path 2 mm past the plate edge; the monitor does not apply a stricter test of its own.
184-- **The object is never read out of the words.** Two messages of one kind are told apart by comparing OrcaSlicer's words now with its words before, as OrcaSlicer does itself. Which object a message is about always comes from a check's own ids.
185-- **A press acts on what is true at the press**, and with no assistant set up it sends nothing and offers the chat panel's setup. **The two buttons differ only in the sentence**: Ask AI and Resolve with AI send the same context and the turn gets the same tools.
186-- **Operation failures are not print issues.** A failed download or a refused arrange is a confirmation, never an entry in the issue list.
187-- **Closing hides, it never resolves.** The pill is always there and is the way back; the list and the bubble are opened and closed, one at a time, and closing either changes nothing about the issue or the count. The list closes on a pick, a second press of the pill, Escape, or a press outside it. The bubble belongs to the selection: opening it selects its object, and it closes when that object stops being selected, which is what a click on the empty plate, Escape and a click on another object already do in OrcaSlicer. Turning the view or dragging the object leaves it open. Its close button leaves the selection alone, and a press on **Ask AI** or **Resolve with AI** that reaches the chat closes it. With one issue the pill opens the bubble directly, and with several the bubble's pager walks them all. The overlay hears Escape and presses through handlers of its own on the canvas's window, bound after OrcaSlicer's and so called first; no OrcaSlicer file is involved.
188-- **Ignoring a warning is the person's mark, not OrcaSlicer's.** **Ignore this warning** in the bubble leaves OrcaSlicer's notification alone: the warning stays in the list, marked, below the ones that count, and the pill stops counting it ("1 warning ignored" when nothing else is left, never "No print issues"). Only a warning can be ignored; a blocker cannot, because OrcaSlicer would still refuse to print. An ignore lasts while OrcaSlicer keeps reporting that warning on the active plate's own list, and is forgotten when OrcaSlicer stops, so a warning that comes back is shown again. It is not saved with the project. The rule is `mark_ignored` in `PrintIssues/PrintIssue`.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.
