## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

### Memory Management
Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Resource management", "[Memory]") {
    auto model = std::make_unique<Model>();
    // Automatic cleanup on test completion/failure
    
    REQUIRE(model->objects.empty());
}
```

TEST_CASE("Performance-sensitive test", "[Performance]") {

content.text:
I've built the sent-print chat note on branch `claude/peaceful-mayer-0dbd04`, but I couldn't check it in the real app. After a successful send from OrcaSlicer's send dialog, a one-line note like "Sent to JusPrin Fake A1 mini · 13:05" appears in the chat and is saved with the project. Nothing is committed, and no OrcaSlicer-owned file was changed.

**How it works:**
- A new listener, `PrintMarkers` in `Shell/PrintMarkers.cpp`, hooks the two public "finished" events OrcaSlicer fires on the Plater (the main slicer view):
  - **print-finished** means the job was sent and started. It becomes "Sent to …".
  - **send-finished** means the file was only stored on the printer. It becomes "Uploaded to … · not started".
- The listener passes each event on to OrcaSlicer's own handler, which still closes the dialog as before.
- A failed send fires neither event, so the error stays in OrcaSlicer's dialog and nothing goes in the chat.
- The note is a new kind of saved chat note that carries:
  - the printer name,
  - the event kind (sent or uploaded),
  - the time,
  - the plate number and name.

  Printer states such as Printing, Paused or Finished can later reuse the same line as new event sources.
- The fake Bambu printer has a new test switch, `"send_fails": true` in `fake_printer.json`, which makes its send fail.

**Verified:**
- **Handler order:** wxWidgets runs the handler bound last first, which I confirmed in its `event.cpp`. So my handler runs before OrcaSlicer's and passes the event on.
- **Build:** the Release build of the app and the test targets succeeds.
- **C++ tests:** agent bridge 448 cases, shell 14, fake Bambu printer 11, all passing.
- **Web tests:** Vitest 616 pass and the TypeScript check is clean.
- **The tests catch breakage:** removing the pass-on call fails the C++ ordering test, and removing the chat-line rendering fails the Vitest marker test.

**Not verified: the real-app send with the fake A1 mini.** The send dialog opened ready to go with Send enabled, but in about ten tries neither clicks nor key presses reached the button. The log never shows `print_job: on_ok to send`. I saw three likely causes:
- A mouse button was left held down after an earlier release attempt was refused. Windows dragged along with the cursor until I released it.
- The modal dialog ended up hidden behind the main window.
- The screen-control tool reported every point of the dialog as belonging to "a different process".

I've closed the scratch app. These screenshots are missing:
1. The chat line after a successful send.
2. A failed send (`send_fails` on), showing the error in the dialog and no chat line.
3. The note still there after reopening the project.

Status and these details are also in the shared notes file `sent-print-ack.md`.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

# CLAUDE.md

JusPrin — a long-lived fork of OrcaSlicer (open-source C++17 3D slicer, wxWidgets GUI, CMake build system).

## Upstream vs. fork attribution

This checkout holds two codebases: upstream OrcaSlicer (the `upstream` remote, SoftFever/OrcaSlicer) and the JusPrin fork's changes on top of it. Fork changes include everything under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and the seams the fork added inside OrcaSlicer-owned files.

- Say "OrcaSlicer does X" only for behavior upstream ships. Behavior added by a fork commit is "JusPrin does X", even when it lives in an OrcaSlicer-owned file.
- Check before attributing; the file path is not enough. Run `git blame` on the line, then `git branch -r --contains <sha> 'upstream/*'`. No upstream branch containing the commit means the fork owns it. Run `git fetch upstream` first if the remote may be stale.
- If you have not checked, say it is unverified whether the behavior is upstream or fork.

## Error handling discipline

- Do not catch an error merely because it can be caught. Catch only when the code can recover, translate the error at an abstraction boundary, or add context that is essential for diagnosis. Logging alone is not recovery.
- Represent expected states with normal control flow, not exceptions.
- Never turn an invariant violation or an "impossible" state into success or a silent no-op. Fix the invalid transition at the layer that owns the decision and let unexpected failures propagate to Sentry.
- Avoid duplicating defensive checks across layers. Keep lower-level operations strict, with their preconditions enforced by the caller that owns the workflow.
- If concurrency makes an invalid state reachable, fix the ordering or synchronization instead of suppressing the resulting error.
- Suppress an error only when it is genuinely expected and safely recoverable; document the reason and cover it with a test. Never broadly swallow unexpected errors.
- Prefer removing the root cause over reducing the visibility of its symptoms. Tests should encode valid transitions and assert that invalid ones remain visible.

## Build Commands

```bash
# macOS
cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Linux
cmake --build build --config RelWithDebInfo --target all --

# Windows (replace %build_type% with Debug/Release/RelWithDebInfo)
cmake --build . --config %build_type% --target ALL_BUILD -- -m
```

Node/npm is required to build the Agent and Home pages, or configure with `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` and supply the bundles.

### Building on a shared machine

Several agent sessions build on the same Mac at once. Without a limit, ninja runs one compile job per core plus two, so every build you start can take the whole machine. In 2026-10 one session stacked four builds in one build directory: 56 clang processes on 12 cores. It kept restarting its build to change targets and never limited the job count.

- Before starting a build, check `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`. If the load is already above the core count, wait or build less.
- Limit jobs: `cmake --build … -- -j4`.
- Decide the full target list before starting. Never restart a running build to add or change targets: let it finish, then build the rest.
- Run one build per build directory. Two ninja processes in one directory compete and can leave its records inconsistent.
- Stopping a build means stopping ninja. `pkill -f "cmake --build …"` kills only the cmake wrapper, and ninja keeps compiling. Start long builds in their own process group (`perl -e 'setpgrp(0,0); exec @ARGV' cmake --build …`) and stop them with `kill -- -<pgid>`. Then confirm with `pgrep -fl ninja` before building again.
- When a build is slow, count your own compile processes before blaming the load on other sessions.
- Reuse an existing build where the task allows. Ask before configuring a fresh full-app build the task does not require.

## Testing

Catch2 framework. Tests in `tests/` directory.

```bash
cd build && ctest --output-on-failure           # all tests
ctest --test-dir ./tests/libslic3r              # individual suite
ctest --test-dir ./tests/fff_print
```

Printer UI without hardware: `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Testing/README.md` (Bambu in-process fake). Isolated `--datadir`; do not drive another JusPrin instance.

## Code Style

- C++17, selective C++20. PascalCase classes, snake_case functions/variables
- `#pragma once` for headers. Smart pointers and RAII preferred
- Parallelization via TBB — be mindful of shared state
- Wording: a file or object is "opened", "imported", "loaded" or "added", never "arrived". "Arrive" is fine for messages, responses, events and lists. `AgentUI/src/wording.test.ts` guards the text the model reads.

## Key Entry Points

- App startup: `src/OrcaSlicer.cpp`
- Slicing pipeline: `src/libslic3r/Print.cpp`
- All print/printer/material settings: `src/libslic3r/PrintConfig.cpp`
- GUI: `src/slic3r/GUI/`
- Core algorithms: `src/libslic3r/` (GCode/, Fill/, Support/, Geometry/, Format/, Arachne/)
- Printer profiles: `resources/profiles/[manufacturer].json`

## JusPrin Production UI

- Start with `agent-docs/jusprin/README.md` for the canonical product definition, production architecture, verification method, Orca integration guidance, and design system.
- Before editing any file outside `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/`, read `agent-docs/jusprin/fork-stewardship.md`. Every line changed in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line this fork re-resolves at every rebase, so those changes must be small, product-neutral, additive where possible, and accompanied by the rebase evidence that document requires.
- Experimental plans, probes, screenshots, logs, and temporary UI code remain on `jusprin-v2-poc`. Use `agent-docs/jusprin/poc-reference.md` for exact commit and path pointers; do not cherry-pick the POC wholesale.
- Curated brand and semantic UI assets live under `resources/jusprin/`.
- Before writing or changing any UI code, native or Agent page, follow "Writing UI code" in `agent-docs/jusprin/design-system.md`: every color, radius, font, and control size comes from the token file through `ShellTheme`, the shell recipes, or the CSS variables. A value with no token gets a token and a guard first, never a literal.
- Temporary working docs (handoffs, findings, plans written for another agent) stay untracked: never commit them, and never add them to `.gitignore` or `.git/info/exclude`. Untracked files in `git status` are how Kenneth tracks work that isn't finished.

## Critical Constraints

- **Backward compatibility required** for .3mf project files and printer profiles
- **Cross-platform** — all changes must work on Windows, macOS, and Linux
- Profile/format changes need version migration handling
- Dependencies built separately in `deps/build/`, then linked to main app

## Code review focus areas

- Changes must not cause regressions in existing functionality, defaults, profiles, or project compatibility.
- Features gated by options must not affect existing behavior when those options are disabled.
- Changes should follow the existing code style and architecture. Architectural changes should be justified in code comments and the PR description.
- Add helper functions or utilities only when existing code cannot reasonably be reused. Avoid duplication.
- Changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files must be additive where possible. Rewriting an upstream function, or reimplementing upstream behavior beside it, needs explicit justification in the PR description.
- When an upstream line is deleted or relocated, say where it went and what a future rebase must carry into the new home.
- Keep code concise and clear. Manually simplify AI generated bloated codes before review.
- Include targeted tests or documented verification for behavior changes, especially in slicing logic, profiles, formats, and GUI defaults.

---
name: live-test-built-app-on-mac
description: "How to launch, see, and drive the locally built JusPrin app on the Mac: the shared bundle id binds tools to the wrong instance, and \"on another Space\" usually means the window is on the second monitor, not that the user is in full screen."
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: fa2d66ed-e217-440b-aae0-da4164953edc
  modified: 2026-09-23T18:10:30.736Z
---

Every build of the fork (and /Applications/OrcaSlicer.app) shares bundle id `com.softfever3d.orca-slicer`. The desktop-control tools resolve an app by bundle id and bind to whichever instance comes first, so `app_list_windows` returns `[]` and filtered screenshots hide the window you actually launched.

**Working recipe (2026-09-05):** `ditto` the built .app into the scratchpad, `plutil -replace CFBundleIdentifier -string com.jusprin.worktree-test`, `codesign --force --deep -s -`, then `open -n <copy>.app --args <model>` and `request_access` for the new id. `app_screenshot`/`app_click` then work and include popup menus. A display-scope `left_click` on the header did NOT open the fork's PopupWindow menus, but a background `app_click` did; take the pixel-level `zoom` with the display tools afterwards (call `app_release` first). Display-scope `Escape` does not close those popups; a click elsewhere does.

The MCP discovery file `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/jusprin/mcp.json` points at the newest instance's `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`; `tests/mcp/probe.py`'s `call()` can drive real tools (e.g. `workspace_inspect`, then `report_slice_review` with sessionId/plateId/sliceResultId) to put the header into the Check-print state without lldb. lldb `expr` cannot call inline accessors like `status_row()`.

**Why:** On 2026-09-01 a verification pass screenshotted the stock app instead of the build; on 2026-09-05 the tools bound to another session's main-repo build.

**How to apply:** Confirm the pid with `pgrep -fl OrcaSlicer.app/Contents/MacOS`; never kill an instance you did not launch. `osascript` System Events by unix id still works to set `frontmost`. See [[jusprin-shell-phase-1-design]] and [[orca-inherited-teardown-crash]].

**"On another Space" usually means "on the other monitor."** Cost about ten turns on
2026-09-09 and produced a wrong report to Kenneth. `app_list_windows` returns
`is_off_space: true` and clicks are refused with "this window is on another Space";
`app_bring_to_current_space` then fails with "the user's current Space is a full-screen
app." Both messages are about Spaces, so the natural read is that the user is sitting in
a full-screen app — but with *Displays have separate Spaces* on, a window merely sitting
on the second monitor produces exactly the same symptoms. Kenneth was not in full screen;
the harness had opened on the Acer.

Tell them apart before saying anything to the user: take a **display-scope** screenshot
(`app_release`, then `computer_batch` screenshot). Its header names the monitor it
captured and lists the others — if the window shows up there, it is a monitor problem,
not a Space problem, and the display-scope tools can drive it immediately. Never conclude
"the user is in a full-screen app" from the background tools' error text alone.

The same flag also flaps: a window can read `is_off_space: false` and click fine, then
read `true` a minute later. Clicks delivered while it is true report `ok ... unverified`
and silently do nothing. **A click that reports "unverified" and changes nothing is not
evidence of an application bug** — on 2026-09-09 that nearly became a filed defect about
being unable to retry after a failed MCP connect. Re-verify on a reachable window before

I still can't get a confirmed send, because none of my clicks or key presses reach OrcaSlicer's "Send print job" dialog. Which monitor the app was on was not the cause. The app is ready for you to press Send yourself, and I'll check the result as soon as you have.

**Where the app is:**
- I checked both monitors by window position. Every JusPrin window is on the laptop screen, which is the main display (1728×1117 points). The external monitor, which now reports as "SB220Q", sits above it at negative coordinates.
- The send dialog is the topmost window at the Send button; nothing covers it.
- The project is open and sliced, and the dialog shows "JusPrin Fake A1 mini(LAN)" ready to send.

**Why my input doesn't reach the dialog:**
- I captured the app's main-thread stack while the dialog was open. OrcaSlicer opens it from a queued event (`Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate`, then `ShowModal`) while wx is running a run-loop callback. Its modal loop then waits for events inside that callback.
- In that state, none of my synthetic mouse clicks or key presses changed the dialog. Clicking Send, toggling Timelapse and pressing Return all did nothing.
- The background click tool refuses the dialog outright: it reports every point as "a different process".
- Normal, non-modal screens work. Clicking a project card on the Home page opened the project, and Cmd+R sliced it.
- So I can't press Send myself. Whether real hardware clicks get through is untested; that is what pressing Send yourself will show.

**Problems I hit on the way:**
- **Wrong launch method:** I had started the app binary directly from my shell. That copy drew its windows but took no input. Launching it with `open -n` fixed that.
- **Permission prompt on startup:** the app's recent-files list pointed into ~/Downloads, which macOS protects. Reading the thumbnails raised a permission prompt that froze startup. I trimmed the list in the scratch app's own settings file rather than answer the prompt, which is your call to make.
- **A separate JusPrin bug:** starting the app with a project file shows the "Previously opened file" prompt during startup. In that state the prompt accepts no input of any kind, so the app sits there for good. I hit this twice. It comes from fork code in `ShellController::install`, called during `post_init`. I have not fixed it, and it should get its own task.

**What happens after you press Send:**
1. I check the log for the send and screenshot the chat line, which should read "Sent to JusPrin Fake A1 mini · HH:MM".
2. I switch the fake printer to `send_fails` and send again, ideally with you pressing Send again. I screenshot the error in the dialog and confirm no chat line appears.
3. I reopen the project to confirm the line was saved with it.

Nothing is committed. The code is unchanged since the last report, and the unit tests and Vitest still pass.

# After Send, nothing says the print went out: options

Working note, 2026-10-28, untracked. Branch checked: `jusprin-newui` at a684aee37d. Critique frames 1A-08 to 1A-12 in https://claude.ai/artifact/XyVvteGiKhiJ6apUx8rcmR.

## The problem

A person slices, presses Print, maps the "?" slot, presses Send in OrcaSlicer's Select Machine dialog and Confirm on its "unknown filaments" warning. The dialog closes and the window looks exactly as before: no line in the chat, nothing on the printer chip or header, the "1 print issue" pill unchanged. The job did go out.

## What I found

**Reproduction.** I launched a scratch copy of the 07:22 build with the fake A1 mini, but the request to control its window was declined, so I did not press Send myself and have no screenshot of my own. The evidence is the walkthrough session's log of the same build and the same steps, earlier today (`debug_Wed_Oct_28_05_47_26_46887.log.0`, lines 17006–17078 and after):

```
05:54:32.001  print_job: on_ok to send
05:54:32.176  FakeBambuAgent: start_local_print file=…/.46887.0.3mf
05:54:32.177  print_job: send ok.
05:54:32.189  skipped tab switch from 1 to 3, lack of network plugins
```

**Where the app learns the result.** On success `PrintJob::process` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/PrintJob.cpp:667`) queues `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` carrying the device id. `Plater::print_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16575`) closes the dialog, selects that machine and asks for OrcaSlicer's **Device** tab. The Plater exposes the event id publicly (`Plater::get_print_finished_event()`, `get_send_finished_event()`), so fork code can bind it without touching OrcaSlicer. The fork binds neither today.

**Why the screen stays the same with the fake.** OrcaSlicer's own acknowledgement is that jump to the Device tab. `Plater::priv::on_tab_selection_changing` (`Plater.cpp:10303`) vetoes it when Bambu's network plug-in isn't loaded. The fake printer doesn't load it, and neither does Kenneth's own config (`installed_networking: false`). That veto is the "skipped tab switch" line above.

**What a real Bambu printer would probably do (from reading the code, not run).** Connecting a real Bambu printer requires the plug-in (`OrcaPrinterBackend.cpp:340`). With the plug-in loaded the jump is not vetoed, and `ShellController::on_page_changed` shows the Notebook on its Device page, the same page as the printer menu's Monitor row. So on real hardware the person probably lands on OrcaSlicer's printer monitor after Send, not on an unchanged screen. **The fake hides this difference.** Whichever option is chosen, someone should check it once on a real printer.

**Failure.** On failure `PrintJob` writes OrcaSlicer's message into the dialog's own status bar (`ctl.show_error_info`, `PrintJob.cpp:658`, shown by `BBLStatusBarPrint`). It posts no event and no notification, and the dialog stays open. A failed send is therefore visible in the dialog but leaves nothing behind once the dialog is closed. The fake always succeeds, so testing failure needs a fork-owned switch in `Testing/FakeBambuAgent.cpp`, for example `"send_fails": true` in `fake_printer.json`.

**The ledger.** `SentRecord`, `add_sent` and `subscribe_ledger` exist, but no production code calls `add_sent` or `add_physical_print` (I grepped all of `src/`). The ledger has no record of this send. So the problem isn't a ledger with no reader; nothing is written at all.

**What the fork already has to build on:**
- `AgentHost::post_note(text, swatch)` adds a one-line note to the active chat, saves it with the project, starts no turn, and is not sent to the model. The header already uses it, through `StatusRow::set_note_sink`, for lines like a printer change. The page draws it as `.message note`.
- The issue pill's confirmations come only from OrcaSlicer's notification list (`NoticeKinds.cpp`, `JUSPRIN_RESULT_KINDS`). A successful print job posts no notification.
- The printer chip makes no claim about the machine. Idle / Printing / Offline appears only on the menu's first row (`PrinterMenu.cpp:84`), read from `MachineObject` when the menu opens.
- Print hosts (Klipper, OctoPrint) already get a chat entry: their upload is a `PrintHostUpload` notification, which `WorkFeed` turns into a work card. Only the Bambu path is silent.

## Options

### A. A one-line chat note when the dialog reports success (recommended)

- **What the person sees:** under the last message, within a second of the dialog closing, `Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2 · 10:42`. It is drawn like the header's change lines, uses the chip's printer name, has no check mark, and stays in the chat and in the saved project. For Bambu's "Send to printer" (upload to storage only, `EVT_SEND_FINISHED`) it says `Uploaded to … · not started`. A failure stays in the dialog as OrcaSlicer shows it today, and the chat gets no line.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. A fork listener binds `get_print_finished_event()` and `get_send_finished_event()` on the Plater, calls `Skip()` so OrcaSlicer's handler still runs, and posts through the note sink the header already uses. This depends on wxWidgets calling the handler bound later first; OrcaSlicer's handler doesn't call `Skip()`. That ordering is unverified here and is the first thing to test. Rebase cost: zero lines. The one dependency is that the two public getters keep existing; they haven't moved in a year.
- **Print history:** this is the history design's chat marker (`▱ Plate 1 · a71f 8c04 → Bambu X1C · 13:06 · history`) without the hash and the link. The same listener is where the history work will write its G-code record and add those two parts. Nothing is thrown away, and notes written before then stay as plain lines.
- **Optional failure line:** a chat line such as `Not sent to … · <OrcaSlicer's reason>` needs OrcaSlicer to report a failure. That means one neutral seam in `PrintJob.cpp`'s failure branch: queue an event with the message, about 4 lines. That file had 23 upstream commits in the past year. I'd leave it out, because the dialog already stays open on the error.

### B. A short confirmation above the issue pill

- **What the person sees:** "Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2" above the pill at the canvas's lower right, with a close button, the same way an export finishing is shown. It disappears when closed and is not in the chat or the saved project.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. The listener from A would push the text through OrcaSlicer's public `NotificationManager::push_notification(text)`, which `NoticeKinds` already routes as a confirmation. But it puts JusPrin's words into the list that the architecture treats as OrcaSlicer's own ("OrcaSlicer's notification list is the source of truth").
- **Print history:** no counterpart. The history design has no toast, so this would be removed or kept alongside the marker later. On real hardware the Device-tab jump also hides the canvas, so the confirmation would usually go unseen.

### C. The printer chip shows "Sending…", then the printer's state

- **What the person sees:** the chip reads Sending… from the press of Send until the job ends, then Printing once the printer reports it. On a LAN send the job takes about 10 ms, so Sending… barely shows. Printing arrives seconds later and only from the printer: the fake never reports it on its own.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** nothing reports the moment Send is pressed. That needs a seam in `SelectMachineDialog::on_send_print`, in a file with 80 upstream commits in the past year. It also reverses the rule that the chip makes no claim about the machine, which is a design change for the chip in every state, not only after a send.
- **Print history:** the history design puts live progress on the printer card and on Print history's "Printing" row, not on the chip. Little of this would carry over.

### D. The agent speaks after the send (app-started turn)

- **What the person sees:** a few seconds later, an assistant message about the send. Nothing appears when no agent is set up, and nothing during a turn already running.
- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. It would use the same listener as A, plus a new skill trigger, the same way `file_loaded` starts a turn today.
- **Against it:** every send costs a model call, the reply is slower than a note, and an acknowledgement that depends on the agent being configured is not an acknowledgement. Product definition §2.9: "The agent learns whether a job went out from the printer's state afterwards, not from the dialog." Under the history design the model reads sends from its state, so it doesn't need to be told.

## Recommendation

**A.** It is instant, it is in the place the person is already looking, it survives with the project, it touches no OrcaSlicer lines, and it is the first piece of the history marker rather than something the history work will remove. Failure stays in OrcaSlicer's dialog, which doesn't close on an error.

A decision that applies to every option: on a real Bambu printer, should OrcaSlicer's jump to its Device page after Send stay (it is OrcaSlicer's own acknowledgement and is reachable from the printer menu today), or should JusPrin keep the person on the project? If it stays, option A's note is what the person sees when they come back. This needs one check on real hardware before anyone relies on it.

## How A would be verified

Add a fork-only fake switch so that `start_local_print` can fail. Then, in the real app with the fake A1 mini: send successfully and screenshot the chat line; send with the switch on and screenshot the dialog's error, with no chat line; reopen the project and check the note is still there. Also add Catch2 coverage that the listener posts exactly one note per success event and none on failure, plus a Vitest check that the note renders.

lines: Rules that follow from the table:

-- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 a project was always open behind Home (the most recent one resumes at startup).

+- A model file never silently lands in whatever project happened to be open behind Home. Before 2026-10-24 Home's Import button did exactly that, because it called OrcaSlicer's `add_model`, and from 2026-09-30 to 2026-10-28 the most recent project reopened behind Home at startup. Home now starts with a blank project behind it, but whatever is open there is still not where a file opened from Home goes.
- A file opened from the OS lands in the running JusPrin. OrcaSlicer's default starts a second process for a .3mf; JusPrin runs as a single instance on every platform.
- Several files opened or dropped together make one new project holding all of them.

- Opening a .3mf as a project is the only thing a .3mf does on the Prepare canvas. Wanting only the geometry out of a .3mf is rare, and the agent or File › Import can do it on request. The one question JusPrin asks on a file open stays the "Previously opened file" question described in the [autosave document](autosave-version-history.md).

- File › Import › Import Zip Archive also reaches `load_files(wxArrayString)`, so a zip on its own keeps OrcaSlicer's behavior and adds. Home's Open… and a drop on Home open a zip in a new project like any model file.

- A file dropped on Home reaches the app as its name and bytes, not its path: the web view takes the drop. On macOS a native drop target on the web view would not see it: wxWidgets 3.3 gives its WebKit view none of the drag methods it gives its own views, so WebKit's own handling runs (read from the wxWidgets source on 2026-10-24; not yet tried with a real drag). The bytes are written to `JusPrin-dropped/<MD5>/<name>` under the system temp folder and opened from there, so the "Previously opened file" question recognizes a .3mf dropped on Home before, but not one first opened from its own folder.
- The agent's tools load through the vector overload of `load_files` and `load_project`, which the seam does not see, and the handler stands aside while a tool's load runs.

+- A 3MF saved for another printer keeps that printer: OrcaSlicer selects the file's system printer profile (a P1S, say) and draws its bed, the person's own printer is not re-selected, and the file's process and filament settings stay as the designer saved them. The header's printer chip is marked "from the file" while the selected profile is not a named printer (decided 2026-10-28, see the design system's Header chip); the agent's load report carries the change (`selectedSetupChange.printerPreset`) and its first message asks which printer to use. OrcaSlicer's "sync the printer information?" question is answered No on every open, since the app stores that answer at startup.
Recent projects appear on Home and in the header menu. Selecting one
opens its managed version even when its imported source file has been removed.
-The most recently authored local project resumes on startup.
+Nothing reopens on startup: the app starts on Home with a blank project behind
+it, and a saved project opens only when the person picks it.

- Functional icons: Lucide artwork at 16, 20, or 24 DIP, colored through the surrounding semantic token, with PNG fallback when the platform path requires it. Do not create a separate UI component for each glyph.

- Setup card (the design system's `PinnedSetupCard`; the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", decided 2026-10-26): the band docked under the chat header, the one place in the Agent pane that is always now. Two parts. Above a 1 DIP `border.subtle` rule, the words someone wrote: the person's purpose in Body Bold, wrapping to two lines and then clipped (the whole of it in the tooltip), and the agent's plan headline in Body Small, `text.primary`; each is present only once written, and with neither the section and its rule are absent, with nothing standing in for them (not the preset name, not the project name, not a hint). Below the rule, OrcaSlicer's facts: the process and first filament presets with "N settings changed" (the project's differences from the presets and the objects' own settings) in Body Small, `text.secondary`, wrapping to two lines and then clipped like the purpose (decided 2026-10-26: at the pane's default width a Bambu preset name with a count overflows one line), and the "All settings" Button/Link, in Body Small Bold, on its first line's baseline; then the time, material and plate figures in Body Small Bold, or the one line that stands in for them ("Not sliced yet" with a Compute estimates link, "Time & material estimates recomputing…"). The eyebrow is "Setup summary" in Label Bold, `action.primary`; the only state beside it is "Agent working". A saved chat's card is the same card in `text.secondary` with the eyebrow "Earlier setup" or "Saved sliced snapshot", a quiet state such as "Saved Oct 3, 10:42" and a footnote line.

-- Setup card warnings: a warning is only an annotation of the one line it contradicts, drawn directly under it, one per line: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` beside Body Small text in `text.primary`. The three in use: "Plan needs another look · <the edit's label>" under the plan (the app's mark after an edit that was not the agent's, cleared only by the agent recording the plan again), "Printer last reported <material>" under the presets, and "Previous estimates · not current" with a Recompute link under the estimates. A warning that names no line of the card is not the card's: print issues belong to the canvas and the chat, nozzle and printer-model mismatches to the header's printer and filament chip. Moments of change ("Updated", the last step with Undo, an estimate before and after, an edit by hand, "Confirmed") are the timeline rows', never the card's.

+- Setup card warnings: a warning is only an annotation of the one line it contradicts, drawn directly under it, one per line: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` beside Body Small text in `text.primary`. The three in use: "Plan needs another look · <the edit's label>" under the plan (the app's mark after an edit that was not the agent's, cleared only by the agent recording the plan again), "Printer last reported <material>" under the presets, and "Previous estimates · not current" with a Recompute link under the estimates. A warning that names no line of the card is not the card's: print issues belong to the canvas and the chat; a mismatch between the selection and the connected machine (its nozzle, its model, what it has loaded) belongs to the chat and to the send dialog, never to the chip (see Header chip). Moments of change ("Updated", the last step with Undo, an estimate before and after, an edit by hand, "Confirmed") are the timeline rows', never the card's.

- Setup card fact glyphs: 14 DIP from `component.setupCard.iconSize`, the one size below the icon scale. The clock, material, plate and warning glyphs sit inside a row of Label text, and a 16 DIP glyph makes that row taller than its text. Do not use this size on another surface; it is not a step of the icon scale.

- Agent message box: one box with the `medium` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke, and `component.composer` insets (8 DIP padding, 4 DIP between staged files, the field, and the toolbar). The field is Body with a 4 DIP inset; it grows a line at a time up to `component.composer.maxLines` (8) and then scrolls, while the toolbar stays visible: the 32 DIP + icon button (or Photo) on the left, Send (`button.primarySmall`, 28 DIP) or Stop (`button.secondarySmall`, 28 DIP) on the right. While the field has the focus the whole box carries the 2 DIP `border.focus` ring. In the app, each + menu choice opens the operating system's file dialog through the host, filtered to that kind. After + come the model and thinking pickers (`button.picker`: 24 DIP, Label, a chevron), which open upward menus no narrower than `component.popover.width`: the model menu lists each set-up provider's models under the provider's name when there is more than one (a provider is added from the Agent settings); the thinking menu lists only the levels the chosen model accepts and is left out when it accepts none. A choice belongs to the chat and applies from its next turn. When the full labels do not fit beside + and Send (the composer measures them, so this follows the labels, not a breakpoint), the thinking picker drops "Thinking:" and shows the level alone; if that still does not fit, the model's name is cut with an ellipsis. Both keep their full name as the accessible name and the tooltip. A model menu of more than 12 models opens with the focus in a Field/Search (`component.fieldSearch`: 38 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that becomes 2 DIP `border.strong` with the focus) inset 8 DIP from the menu's sides; the menu is then `component.popover.width` wide and its rows scroll under the field. Typing filters on the model or provider name, ignoring case, the first match carries the menu-row hover fill, Up and Down move it, Enter picks it, and Escape clears the field before it closes the menu. A provider with more than 12 models shows its count beside its name while nothing is typed.

- All settings panel (the "JusPrin v2" canvas, page "Current Setup Card", the four "All settings" boards): opened from the "All settings" link at the end of the setup card's presets line, it takes the Agent pane's place under a header of the compact icon button back to the chat, the title in Body Bold and the pane's own toggle. A "Showing" row holds the design system's Select (`component.select`: 26 DIP, `small` radius, Body text, a 16 DIP chevron, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke that strengthens on hover and becomes the focus ring when open; its menu is the Menu/Popover under its left edge, as wide as the field) listing the whole project, each plate when there are two or more, and each object; it follows the selection in the 3D view. Under it a Field/Search ("Search settings") beside an All / Changed Segmented Control. The presets in use sit in a `surface.subtle` box with the `medium` radius, each filament slot with its Swatch (`component.swatch`, 24 DIP, `small` radius, a 1 DIP `border.subtle` inside stroke). Groups are OrcaSlicer's own pages (Quality, Strength, Speed, Support, Multimaterial, Others, then Filament and Printer) with a 32 DIP header row (16 DIP chevron, Body Small Bold name, Label summary at the right) and rows indented 24 DIP: Body Small name and value on a 28 DIP line, a changed value in Body Small Bold with "Preset: …" in Metadata under it. Two or three filament slots stand side by side, one column per slot; more than three go through a slot picker, one at a time. The host reads the whole table in one message (`settings_catalog`, the `all_settings` capability). Only one object's view has anything to press: a Button/Link at the end of a row's note, under the value, where the table marks one — "Use project value" under a setting the object, a part, a modifier or a height range sets itself (not a range's own layer height or filament, which define it), and "Remove" under its support blockers or enforcers. Each press is one OrcaSlicer undo step of the person's, named for what it did, and the panel redraws from the host's next table (`settings_action`, the `settings_actions` capability).
- Link button: 26 DIP high, 4 DIP horizontal padding, Label Bold in `action.primary`, underlined on hover (`component.button.link`).

- Segmented control: a 30 DIP `surface.subtle` track with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` border and 2 DIP padding, holding 24 DIP segments in Label; the chosen one is `action.primary` (`component.segmented`).

- Tooltip: 24 DIP high, 4×8 DIP padding, Metadata, inverse (`text.primary` fill, `surface.canvas` text) with the subtle elevation (`component.tooltip`). Native tooltips are the operating system's own.

+- Header chip: 28 DIP high, `chip` radius (`component.chip`). The chip states the selection: the printer profile the project will be sliced for, its nozzle, the project's filaments. It may qualify that statement, and must, when the plain statement would mislead; the qualification is about the selection itself, comes from OrcaSlicer's own state, and holds regardless of what the chat says. The chip makes no claim about the physical machine: what is loaded, which plate is on, which nozzle is fitted, whether it is connected or busy. Those belong to the chat, the setup card's line annotations, the printer menu's first row, and the send dialog. The chat never changes the chip. (Kenneth, 2026-09-06, restated 2026-10-28: the September rule "the chip states facts and never warns" was about the chat steering the chip and about mismatches with the connected machine; it was not about the selection.) Four tests for any mark proposed for the chip:
+  1. Is it about the selection or about the machine? Machine means not on the chip.
+  2. Would the chip's plain text mislead without it? If not, it is a warning, and warnings go to the chat.
+  3. Does it come from OrcaSlicer's preset state, or from an observation or a judgement? Observations and judgements go to the chat.
+  4. Can the chat create or clear it? If yes, it is not the chip's.

+  The one mark in use passes all four. Its printer half is marked while the selected printer profile is not one of the person's named printers and not OrcaSlicer's placeholder (`Printers::printer_from_file`), which is what opening a 3MF saved for another printer leaves selected: the 14 DIP `triangle-alert` glyph in `status.warning` takes the printer glyph's place, the label reads "<model> · <nozzle> · from the file" in `text.primary`, and the tooltip names the file. The chip's menu then opens with that printer and the Body Small line "From the file · not one of your printers", a row that cannot be pressed; every other row is the stock menu. Nothing is stored: the mark goes when a named printer is selected, from the menu or by the agent. Decided 2026-10-28; boards 1 to 5 of "File for another printer" on the canvas's Printer & Material Settings page.

- Reply choice (Chat/Reply Choice): drawn as a reply the person could send, not as an app control. 28 DIP high with `component.replyChip` padding, the `full` radius (the one capsule control), Body `text.primary` on `surface.subtle` (the person's own bubble) with a 1 DIP `border.subtle` stroke; hover and pressed go to `surface.selected`, never `action.primary`. A tapped choice is sent as the person's bubble in the same tint and words.
- Expanded button: at least 32 DIP high, 12×8 DIP padding, 4 DIP radius.

- Plates / Project pane: 200 DIP wide on `surface.subtle`, a 12 DIP band above a 36 DIP tab strip (the active tab is Label Bold with a 2 DIP `action.primary` rule; the other is Label in `text.secondary`). Plate rows are 32 DIP, object rows 36 DIP, both on `surface.canvas` blocks with the standard radius and a 2 DIP gap; a folded plate adds a 20 DIP Metadata summary line indented 32 DIP. Every number is under `component.leftPane`, taken from the boards on the canvas's Plates & Project Pane page.

content.content:
Kenneth Jiang Wed Oct 28 18:54:15 2026 +0000
Print history: record every G-code that leaves a project, show it, print it again

One record per G-code that left a project replaces the Sent events and
physical prints, which nothing outside tests ever wrote. It is shown on one
Print history screen, and any recorded G-code can be printed again from the
file the project kept. Nothing records, badges or draws a failure: a
printer reports a person's stop and a failed print the same way, so a print
that ended early simply never finishes. Slicing writes nothing.

The record (Agent/ManufacturingHistory, Agent/ProjectStateDocument)
- Keyed by the SHA-256 of the plate's sliced G-code, so the same slice
  exported and sent is one record. It holds where the G-code went (exports
  with the exported file's own hash; sends with the printer's name, whether
  the send started the print, when the transport confirmed it, and for a
  Bambu send the hash of the package it uploaded) and the prints the
  printer reported: started, finished. It also holds the slice's estimates
  and layer count, the presets, and the chat item it followed.
- A copy of each G-code that leaves is kept at <project>/gcode/<hash>.gcode,
  the newest 20 per project. A Bambu print also keeps the .gcode.3mf it
  uploaded, byte for byte (and for a cloud printer the config 3MF it also
  sent), pruned with its G-code.
- A document holding the old "sent" and "physicalPrints" arrays loads and
  drops them (no shipped build wrote them).

Writers (Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder)
- Exports (OrcaSlicer's own and the export_file tool's) through the new
  EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED; Bambu prints and uploads through the jobs' finished
  events while their dialog is showing; print-host uploads through the
  queue's new enqueue observer and the queue dialog's progress at 100.
- Bambu printers are polled every two seconds whatever is on screen;
  Agent/PrintOutcomeTracker decides which report belongs to which send, and
  a finish of a project that is not open is written into its saved
  document. Print hosts record sends only.

Print history (HomeUI, Home/PrintHistory, Home/OrcaHomeBackend)
- A second screen of the Home page: one entry per G-code, grouped by day,
  with a row per destination (an export: matches, changed outside JusPrin,
  not found; a send: delivery and whether it started) and per print
  (Printing with its progress, Finished; a stopped one shows only when it
  started). Project and printer are removable filter chips over one list,
  with a search box. Its bar is Back and the title: Preferences is reached
  from the title bar's menu and Ctrl+, (Cmd+, on macOS).
- Ways in: a link in the gallery header, a line on each project card and
  printer card, one row on the project pane's Project tab (replacing its
  old Print history view), and a "history" link on each chat marker. Back
  returns to where it was opened from.
- Open in chat opens the project and scrolls its chat to the marker
  (reveal_item). Export... writes the kept copy and records it; Export again
  on a changed file writes a new file beside it, never over it.
- The chat shows one marker line where a G-code left, in place of the
  retired print card. The model reads the last ten records as printHistory.

Print again, and print_dialog_open
- Sends the kept file, never a fresh slice, always through OrcaSlicer's own
  send dialog; the person presses Send there and nothing in it is set.
- Bambu: the kept package goes to Select Machine the way the printer's file
  browser opens a file (Plater::update_print_required_data,
  EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW), with the dialog's new-print flag set so the
  job uploads the local file as a new print. Printing from the printer's

content.content:
20:**Where the app learns the result.** On success `PrintJob::process` (`src/slic3r/GUI/Jobs/PrintJob.cpp:667`) queues `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` carrying the device id. `Plater::print_job_finished` (`Plater.cpp:16575`) closes the dialog, selects that machine and asks for OrcaSlicer's **Device** tab. The Plater exposes the event id publicly (`Plater::get_print_finished_event()`, `get_send_finished_event()`), so fork code can bind it without touching OrcaSlicer. The fork binds neither today.
22:**Why the screen stays the same with the fake.** OrcaSlicer's own acknowledgement is that jump to the Device tab. `Plater::priv::on_tab_selection_changing` (`Plater.cpp:10303`) vetoes it when Bambu's network plug-in isn't loaded. The fake printer doesn't load it, and neither does Kenneth's own config (`installed_networking: false`). That veto is the "skipped tab switch" line above.
31:- `AgentHost::post_note(text, swatch)` adds a one-line note to the active chat, saves it with the project, starts no turn, and is not sent to the model. The header already uses it, through `StatusRow::set_note_sink`, for lines like a printer change. The page draws it as `.message note`.
41:- **OrcaSlicer lines:** none. A fork listener binds `get_print_finished_event()` and `get_send_finished_event()` on the Plater, calls `Skip()` so OrcaSlicer's handler still runs, and posts through the note sink the header already uses. This depends on wxWidgets calling the handler bound later first; OrcaSlicer's handler doesn't call `Skip()`. That ordering is unverified here and is the first thing to test. Rebase cost: zero lines. The one dependency is that the two public getters keep existing; they haven't moved in a year.
49:- **Print history:** no counterpart. The history design has no toast, so this would be removed or kept alongside the marker later. On real hardware the Device-tab jump also hides the canvas, so the confirmation would usually go unseen.
53:- **What the person sees:** the chip reads Sending… from the press of Send until the job ends, then Printing once the printer reports it. On a LAN send the job takes about 10 ms, so Sending… barely shows. Printing arrives seconds later and only from the printer: the fake never reports it on its own.
59:- **What the person sees:** a few seconds later, an assistant message about the send. Nothing appears when no agent is set up, and nothing during a turn already running.
71:Add a fork-only fake switch so that `start_local_print` can fail. Then, in the real app with the fake A1 mini: send successfully and screenshot the chat line; send with the switch on and screenshot the dialog's error, with no chat line; reopen the project and check the note is still there. Also add Catch2 coverage that the listener posts exactly one note per success event and none on failure, plus a Vitest check that the note renders.

content.text:
The decision that reached me settled what happens on a send and deliberately left printer events like a failed print for later. It said nothing about what happens when there's no active chat. If you discussed that in the parent session, "Common Jusprin user flows", it didn't reach me.

**What was decided.** The parent session relayed this from you after you said "go with this approach":
- **Option A:** after a send, one dated line appears in the chat, such as "Sent to Bambu Lab A1 mini 2 · 10:42". If the file was only stored on the printer, it reads "Uploaded to … · not started".
- **One reusable marker type.** It is for events that happen outside the project. It records the printer name, the kind of event, the time and the plate.
- **In scope now:** only the sent and uploaded cases.
- **Later, not wired now:** the printer's own state changes, "Printing", "Paused", "Failed" and "Finished". The marker was built so these can be added later as new event sources without a new kind of line.
- **A failed send:** OrcaSlicer's dialog shows the error and the chat says nothing. This is the send itself failing, not a print failing later on the printer.
- **Other rules:** the note is saved with the project, and no OrcaSlicer files change.

**What wasn't decided:**
1. **Failed prints and other printer events** arrive later, after the send. They were explicitly deferred. Nothing in my commit listens to the printer after the send.
2. **No active chat.** This wasn't part of the decision. From reading the code, without testing it: my note goes to the project's *active* chat. If the project has no active chat, the save step silently does nothing, yet the page is still told about the new line. So the line could appear and then vanish when the project is reopened. I also don't know whether a project can be open with no active chat in practice. Separately, if you're viewing a different chat than the active one, the line goes to the active one, not the one in front of you.

**The print-history commit.** Your commit on origin today, ebbb2f8894, already adds a chat marker where a G-code leaves the project. It also tracks printer reports after a send: it polls Bambu printers and records started and finished prints. So it covers part of point 1, which my commit never did. I haven't checked how it handles no active chat.

That's why I still think dropping my commit is the right call. The open question, if you want it settled, is how print history's marker behaves with no active chat. That's a check against its code, not mine.

+The ledger is the project's G-code records (`Agent/ManufacturingHistory.hpp`): one record per G-code that left the project, keyed by the SHA-256 of the plate's sliced G-code, holding where it went (exports, sends) and the prints the printer reported (started, finished; never a failure). Slicing writes nothing. It can have any number of subscribers, through `ProjectPersistence::subscribe_ledger`. The pane and the header's overflow menu each subscribe to it separately.

+`Shell/GcodeHistoryRecorder` writes the records where OrcaSlicer already says a file left: `EVT_OUTPUT_EXPORTED` for an export (OrcaSlicer's own and the `export_file` tool's), the Bambu print and send jobs' finished events while their dialog is showing, and the print-host queue's enqueue observer followed by the queue dialog's progress at 100. Each time, a copy of the G-code is kept at `<project>/gcode/<hash>.gcode` (the last `kKeptGcodeCopies` per project). It polls Bambu printers every two seconds whatever is on screen; `Agent/PrintOutcomeTracker` decides which report belongs to which send, and a finish of a project that is not open is written into that project's saved document.
