A skill with a trigger is the app's: when the event it names happens, the host adds it to the one request where the model first reads about the event, as the request's last item, and to no later request. A skill with a description is the model's: `skill_read` lists the described skills in its own description and returns one by name, and is offered only while at least one exists. One skill has a description and a trigger: `calibration`, read when a print problem may come from the filament or its settings, when the person asks to calibrate, or in a calibration project, and fired by `calibration_started` on the first turn of a calibration project's chat; it carries the conversation of a calibration (when a test is worth it, the two facts said before the person's project closes, asking which test only when the handover leaves it open, per-test ranges and how to read the print, the naming rule for the saved preset), while `calibration_generate`'s description keeps only that tool's rules. Four other skills have triggers, one file each:

- `file-loaded` (trigger `file_loaded`): the first message after a file is opened or imported is a judgement about the load report. It fires when the person opens or drops a file, after an in-app `object_import` (and a failed `project_open`) in the same turn, and in the opened project's chat after an in-app `project_open`, which replaces the conversation and so ends the turn that asked. An MCP client's loads fire nothing. The host sends a picture of the active plate with it and, when no purpose is recorded, one sentence of its own built from that state.

-- `project-setup-changed` (trigger `setup_changed`): check the setup in force against the print's purpose. It fires on the result of an in-app `setup_record` that recorded a purpose for the first time or changed it (its result says which in `purposeChange`; a call that restates the same purpose, or leaves it out, to change the plan does not fire it), when the printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the setup the model was last asked to check under a recorded purpose (on the next tool result of the turn, or on the next turn's first request when the person changed it by hand), and on a turn's first request after the person restored an earlier version while a purpose is recorded. Each time the model is asked to check, the app saves the setup in force as the one checked. The model's own successful `printer_setup` fires nothing: the setup it chose is saved as checked at once (Kenneth, 2026-10-19), so the skill is for a setup that moved without the model, and a pairing its change breaks is caught by the slice-refusal facts and skill. It gives way to the file-loaded skill on a request that carries both, since that skill already asks for the same check.

+- `project-setup-changed` (trigger `setup_changed`): check the setup in force against the print's purpose. It fires on the result of an in-app `setup_record` that recorded a purpose for the first time or changed it (its result says which in `purposeChange`; a call that restates the same purpose, or leaves it out, to change the plan does not fire it), when the printer, filament, process or plate type differs from the setup the model was last asked to check under a recorded purpose (on the next tool result of the turn, or on the next turn's first request when the person changed it by hand), on a turn's first request after the person restored an earlier version while a purpose is recorded, and on every turn's first request while the plan is marked `needs_reassessment` (2026-10-28: the model may leave recording the plan to the turn that answers its question about the change, and that turn finds the setup checked already, so without this the mark could outlive every skill that explains it). Each time the model is asked to check, the app saves the setup in force as the one checked. The model's own successful `printer_setup` fires nothing: the setup it chose is saved as checked at once (Kenneth, 2026-10-19), so the skill is for a setup that moved without the model, and a pairing its change breaks is caught by the slice-refusal facts and skill. It gives way to the file-loaded skill on a request that carries both, since that skill already asks for the same check.

- `slice-failed` (trigger `slice_failed`): a plate's last slice did not succeed, because OrcaSlicer's check refused the plate or the run failed. The adapter records why on the plate (`WorkspacePlate::slice_failure`: refused or failed, OrcaSlicer's words, the setting and object when named) at the moment it happens (a hook in `Plater::reslice`, `Workspace/SliceRequests.hpp`, and the run's completion event), worded by the print-issue monitor's `slice_failure_of`, and keeps it until the plate slices. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceFailure`; `slice_report` of an unsliced plate adds the check code and the object's name. The skill fires once per failure, on the first request that carries it: the result of the model's own `slice_start`, the turn the app starts when a slice the model started fails after its turn, or the next message after the person's Slice all. The same refusal again is the same failure.

-- `print-issues` (trigger `print_issues`): what the print-issue chip's two buttons ask for and how to read what OrcaSlicer reports. The adapter reads a slice's warnings through the monitor's `slice_warnings_of` while the plate is active and keeps a summary on the plate while that slice is current (`WorkspacePlate::slice_warnings`: the count, how many the person ignored, and the first warning, critical first, in OrcaSlicer's words with its setting and object). It counts every warning the chip lists, so the bed-temperature warning too, which `slice_report` leaves out. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceWarnings`. The skill fires on the request that carries a chip's message, and on the first request whose workspace shows warnings no request has carried yet, whether the person sliced (their next message) or the model did (the tool result that shows them, or the app's turn when its slice ended after its turn); a re-slice with the same warnings fires nothing.

+- `print-issues` (trigger `print_issues`): what the print-issue chip's Ask AI button asks for and how to read what OrcaSlicer reports. The adapter reads a slice's warnings through the monitor's `slice_warnings_of` while the plate is active and keeps a summary on the plate while that slice is current (`WorkspacePlate::slice_warnings`: the count, how many the person ignored, and the first warning, critical first, in OrcaSlicer's words with its setting and object). It counts every warning the chip lists. The chip and `slice_report` read the same slice-result rule (`Workspace/SliceResultWarnings`), so they list the same warnings, except that `slice_report` also lists the timelapse ones, marked `appliesWhen: "timelapse"`, which the chip does not count. Every request carries it as the plate's `sliceWarnings`. The skill fires on the request that carries a chip's message, and on the first request whose workspace shows warnings no request has carried yet, whether the person sliced (their next message) or the model did (the tool result that shows them, or the app's turn when its slice ended after its turn); a re-slice with the same warnings fires nothing.

-| `print_dialog_open` | M | Opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog for one plate, the way Print does: Select Machine for a printer on Bambu's network, the upload dialog for a print host. Called only when the person asks to print; getting a print ready never opens it. Refused with `needs_step` naming `slice_start` when the plate has no valid slice. The dialog fills itself in (printer, slot mapping, options last used for that printer model); the call sets nothing in it. The dialog is modal, so the call returns once it is shown, before its modal loop starts, and reports nothing about a send: the person presses Send there. Changes no project state. | `Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate`; `Plater::send_gcode_legacy` | |

+| `print_dialog_open` | M | Opens OrcaSlicer's send dialog for one plate, the way Print does: Select Machine for a printer on Bambu's network, the upload dialog for a print host. Called only when the person asks to print; getting a print ready never opens it. Refused with `needs_step` naming `slice_start` when the plate has no valid slice. Implemented, in-app and over MCP. With `gcode` (a G-code hash or its leading 8+ digits, as `printHistory` gives it) it prints that recorded G-code again from the file the project kept, not a fresh slice: a Bambu printer is sent the `.gcode.3mf` an earlier Bambu send uploaded (Select Machine in its print-from-storage mode, with its new-print flag, so it uploads the local file), a print host with OrcaSlicer's standard upload dialog the kept G-code. Refused (`refused`, `no_printer`) when the file is gone, changed on disk, or not kept for the printer selected now. The dialog fills itself in (printer, slot mapping, options last used for that printer model); the call sets nothing in it. The dialog is modal, so the call returns once it is shown, before its modal loop starts, and reports nothing about a send: the person presses Send there. Changes no project state. | `Plater::priv::on_action_print_plate`; `Plater::send_gcode_legacy`; `Plater::update_print_required_data` and `EVT_PRINT_FROM_SDCARD_VIEW`; `SelectMachineDialog::set_required_data_new_print` | |

| `export_file` | D | G-code, sliced 3mf, project 3mf, STL, or preset bundle to a path. Validation surfaces license restrictions from project details in the result and on the activity card. | `Plater` export functions | |
-### A send's outcome is two Plater events, and only on success
-OrcaSlicer's Bambu send dialogs run a job on their own worker. On success the
-job queues one event on the Plater: `EVT_PRINT_FINISHED` from Select Machine
-(`PrintJob`, the event's string is the device id) and `EVT_SEND_FINISHED` from
-Send to Printer (`SendJob`, storage only; the string is the project name).
-Neither event is declared in a header, but `Plater::get_print_finished_event()`
-and `get_send_finished_event()` return their ids, so fork code binds them with
-no OrcaSlicer line. OrcaSlicer's handlers close the dialog and do not skip; a
-handler bound later runs first and must `Skip()` (`Shell/PrintMarkers`).
-A failed job queues nothing and posts no notification: its words go to the
-dialog's own status bar, and the dialog stays open.
-`Plater::print_job_finished` also asks for OrcaSlicer's Device tab.
-`on_tab_selection_changing` vetoes that switch while Bambu's network plug-in
-is not loaded ("skipped tab switch … lack of network plugins"), which is the
-case with the fake Bambu printer. A real Bambu printer needs the plug-in to
-connect, so there the switch is expected to happen. That has not been checked
